cards.title: Base Labs launches AI safety partnership with Hugging Face
cards.body: Base Labs, spun up by Baseten, will develop and publish methods for training and monitoring open models. The partnership aims to advance responsible AI development practices.

cards.title: Pinterest launches AI-powered Restyle room design feature
cards.body: The new feature lets users visualize furniture, decor, and lighting in photos of their own rooms. It's designed to help turn saved inspiration into actual purchases.

cards.title: Huawei accelerates Q1 2027 AI chip launch
cards.body: The next-generation Ascend 960DT chip will compete directly with Nvidia. Huawei aims to close China's AI computing gap with the U.S.

cards.title: AI agents Instinct and Muse add call capabilities
cards.body: Both assistants can now make restaurant reservations and cancel subscriptions. The feature expands their practical utility for everyday tasks.

cards.title: Google, Nvidia, Anthropic form Emerald AI coalition
cards.body: The group aims to find 100 GW of grid capacity for new data centers. The initiative addresses critical infrastructure needs for expanding AI operations.

cards.title: Iceland's Treble raises $18M for voice simulation
cards.body: Treble's platform is used by voice AI developers and robotics companies. The funding accelerates growth in the voice AI space.

cards.title: Google launches MCP server for AI-controlled smart homes
cards.body: AI agents like Claude and ChatGPT can now control Google Home devices and access camera summaries. The early access program expands AI integration into household automation.

cards.title: Anthropic merges Claude chat and Cowork interface
cards.body: The unified platform is launching for Pro and Max subscribers. It streamlines the user experience across chat and collaboration features.

cards.title: Anthropic and OpenAI embed safety evaluators in labs
cards.body: Both companies are hiring independent safety evaluators for unprecedented lab access. Researchers welcome the move but stress the need for transparency and eventual regulation.

cards.title: Meta prepares camera-free Ray-Ban glasses
cards.body: Meta is developing a version without a camera to address privacy concerns. The move follows accusations about the original glasses' privacy implications.

cards.title: Threads adds tools for podcast promotion
cards.body: New features include profile cards, episode links, transcripts, guest tags, and audience insights. Meta is positioning Threads as a podcast hub to rival Twitter.

cards.title: Snap justifies $2,200 Specs smart glasses
cards.body: Snap continues to explain the value proposition of its premium smart glasses. The company launched Specs earlier this year and is seeking broader adoption.

cards.title: Al Gore: Real AI risk isn't data centers
cards.body: Gore expressed greater concern about AI industry's own warnings on technology trajectory. He downplayed data center emissions as the primary concern.

cards.title: SK Hynix in talks with Intel on US chips
cards.body: SK Hynix is considering building memory chips in the United States. The company told TechCrunch no final plans have been finalized.

cards.title: Building the materials foundation for AI
cards.body: As AI pushes computing into new territory, semiconductors and data centers are approaching physical limits. Materials science is becoming just as crucial as the algorithms themselves for supporting AI infrastructure.

cards.title: AI's trillion-dollar gamble and economic impact
cards.body: Finance professors are assessing AI's real economic impact over the next few years amid significant uncertainties. The trillion-dollar question looms: can AI deliver on its promised productivity gains?

cards.title: OpenAI paying for biology data to train models
cards.body: OpenAI is bidding at biotech company bankruptcies to acquire detailed regulatory and manufacturing data for AI systems. This strategy aims to supercharge medical AI models with real-world biological information.

cards.title: AI industry leaders warn of extinction risks
cards.body: Dario Amodei, Sam Altman, Elon Musk, and Demis Hassabis are now aligned on advanced AI dangers. Employees at leading AI labs believe there's a real possibility that advanced AI could destroy humanity.

cards.title: AI doomers call for brakes on LLM development
cards.body: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei posted an essay calling for slower development of large language models due to looming dangers. The AI industry has shifted toward acknowledging existential risks from rapid advancement.

cards.title: Apple building AI server with M-series chips
cards.body: Apple is reportedly developing a server packed with M-series Ultra chips designed for AI workloads. This move signals Apple's strategy to build custom silicon for on-device and server-based AI.
